subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: I notice that article VI of the convention refers to territorial waters. What does the Department of Transport consider to be the territorial waters of Canada?

speakerposition: Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Transport
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Three miles.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext:
Here is another illustration of the need for Canada to make up her mind about her territorial waters. For several years the Department of Fisheries has been trying to get a definition of Canadian territorial waters which will meet the actual needs of the country today. We seem to go along year after year without making a decision on this point, expecting that some day there will be an international treaty under which all nations will agree to just what constitutes territorial waters.
From what I read about the situation there seems to be very little prospect of any agreement being reached on that point in the near future. In the meantime various countries

are making declarations as to what they consider to be their territorial waters. I suggest to the Prime Minister that it is about time Canada made up her mind as to what Canadian territorial waters are to be. Here we are becoming a party to a convention which refers to territorial waters, and surely there should be some clarification of what this government considers to be Canadian territorial waters.
I believe the Prime Minister knows that on the east coast they are asking for a 12-mile limit. They are in trouble with their fisheries because there is no 12-mile limit and our fishermen are being unfairly treated. On the west coast we have the situation created by Hecate strait between the Queen Charlotte islands and the mainland of British Columbia. This should be considered Canadian territorial waters, yet these waters have not been positively declared as such.
Frankly I cannot see why the government delays in taking a stand on this question. I think it is just chasing a will o' the wisp to be waiting year after year for some kind of international agreement. I hope something will be done this year by the government, and that there will not be any further delay in reaching a decision as to just what constitutes Canadian territorial waters.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: The matter is now under very active consideration. We do not want to make a declaration at this time which would call for contestation by our friends. We are endeavouring to arrange matters so that we can make our declaration and not have it contested by adjoining countries, and countries with whom we have always had cordial relations.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: When does the Prime Minister expect that this declaration will be made?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: There is to be a discussion on this matter at the next general assembly of the United Nations. We hope that before that time we will be able to inform these adjoining and friendly powers of the position we are going to endeavour to promote at this meeting of the United Nations.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Will that be made public at the time or will it all be confidential?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: The communications we are having with these friendly powers at this time are confidential, but the agenda for the next meeting of the United Nations provides for a public discussion at which time we would be taking our position on several of the controversial points.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Will that constitute a declaration by Canada as to what she considers her territorial waters to be?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext:
I do not
know that a declaration by Canada as to what she considers her territorial waters to be would advance us very much unless we got a recognition from others that they would respect those territorial limitations.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Is it not a fact that quite a few other countries have made unilateral declarations as to what they consider their territorial waters to be, and apparently in most cases those declarations are respected by other nations?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: They are not; they are contested. The matter is being considered now by an international committee which was set up by the United Nations and which will be making its report. I hope and expect there will be discussion on that report, at which time many governments will be making their positions clearly known.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: I gather from what the Prime Minister said that at the United Nations the Canadian government would try to indicate, would endeavour to propose-

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Would endeavour to promote an international theory as to the extent of territorial waters and the way in which they are to be determined from point to point.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: The Prime Minister is saying that at this international gathering we would endeavour to propose. What in the world is stopping Canada from standing on her two feet and making a proposition? Why do we have to endeavour to propose?

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Because of the number of divisions we have in our armed forces. We do not want to start a war. We think the method we are following is the one that is most apt to get recognition without any conflict as to what will be regarded internationally as the territorial waters.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: There are two different things. One is making a declaration of something you are going to do, and another is making a proposition of what you think is a fair attitude. The Prime Minister said they were going to endeavour to make a proposal.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Not endeavour to make a proposal.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext:
You cannot stand up and make a proposal regarding what Canada thinks should or should not be done and ask other people in a straightforward manner whether or not they agree with that, or do we always have to be mealy-mouthed in our attitude to other nations?
Canada Shipping Act

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext:
We do not
have to be mealy-mouthed, but we do not find that it would be of serious advantage to adopt the attitude of the hon. member.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: As I understand it, the Prime Minister is referring to discussions of this question which will probably take place in the general assembly of the United Nations later this year. I presume those discussions would be among all the nations that are members of the United Nations, but does that mean that no decision will be reached by Canada unless all these nations agreed to a definition of territorial waters?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Canada itself cannot enact international law, but Canada will use its best endeavours to get recognized as international law the principles for which we shall be contending.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext:
I should think it very unlikely that all these nations would reach any agreement, because they are so very far apart. As the Prime Minister knows, there are different limits set by many different nations. It is not a matter of war at all; it is simply a matter of what these nations consider to be their territorial waters. For example, I believe some of the nations in South America claim that their territorial waters run out for 200 miles. Will Canada not be in the position, if the Prime Minister's course is followed, that she simply goes to the meeting of United Nations and puts forward her suggestions; then, if no agreement is reached, shall we not be back exactly where we started?
Does there not come a time when Canada, as I believe Australia and many other nations have done, can and should say that Canada considers her territorial waters to be 12 miles from the shore line estimated in such and such a way? Will it not be necessary for Canada to take that step at some time, in any event, if there is ever to be any definition of Canadian territorial waters?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext:
We shall certainly say what we consider should be regarded and recognized internationally as Canadian territorial waters, but we do not want to start something that we are not in a position to carry through. We shall have to have, not the unanimous consent of all the United Nations, but we shall have to have recognition by, for example, the authorities of the United States, the authorities of France and the authorities of those countries who have historic fishing rights on the great banks. We should have, by general recognition to make it regarded as binding upon all nations, acceptance of the decision that was

Canada Shipping Act rendered by the international court of justice with respect to the conflict between northern European countries and the United Kingdom. That has set a principle which we think should be applicable to our own shores. We think the conditions are such that the decision that was there rendered would apply to many parts of the Canadian shores, and we think this effort by the United Nations to clarify the international law in that regard is very much worth while.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: May I take it from the Prime Minister's replies that the Canadian government has already decided what it considers should be Canadian territorial waters?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: -and is merely waiting for an opportunity to place that opinion before the general assembly of the United Nations?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: I should not like to say that there has been a firm decision that may not be varied as a consequence of our conferring with the other nations, but we think, for example, that this decision of the international court of justice is applicable to most of our shore line. We think the 12-mile limit should be recognized, but we must admit that even if it is there are historic fishing rights that we shall also have to recognize within those territorial waters.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Are those not separate things? Are not the historic fishing rights one thing and the question of territorial waters another thing?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: It will be helpful, I think, to have those matters discussed at the same time and, in order to get recognition of our claims, to have our claims qualified by the knowledge given to those who might be disposed to contest them that it is not intended thereby to exclude the historic fishing rights that have been established over the centuries.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext:
While we are on this subject, I too should like to address a question to the Prime Minister about it. I have in my hand an extract from the Times of London for June 8 last, as quoted in the July 13 issue of the fisheries council of Canada Bulletin. This extract says in part:
The international law commission today finally confessed its failure to be able to agree on a firm formula regulating the breadth of the territorial sea.
It goes on to set forth some details and then states:
The commission recognizes that international practice is not uniform as regards the delimitation of the territorial sea. The commission considers that international law does not permit an extension of the territorial sea beyond 12 miles . . .


Then it goes on at the end of this extract to say:
Members were probably influenced in their final vote by a serious warning sounded by Sir Gerald Fitzmaurice (United Kingdom) against a general licensing of the 12-mile limit.
In view of our close relationship with the United Kingdom within the commonwealth, and in view of the general expression of support for the 12-mile limit by the Prime Minister, I wonder whether he could tell us whether there are any direct discussions going on with the United Kingdom, and could he perhaps give us some information as to why apparently the United Kingdom is so much opposed to this extension, with which I think most of the people in this country agree?

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: On a point of order, are not these territorial waters more a concern of the Department of Fisheries?

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: On the point of order, this very convention we are considering refers to territorial waters, and this whole discussion has been completely in order, if the hon. member had only been listening.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: I would not attempt to state what are the reasons of the United Kingdom for desiring to maintain the territorial waters within the three-mile limitation. They are probably the same reasons they had for supporting that stand before the international court of justice.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: My question was whether the Canadian government is carrying on any direct discussions with the United Kingdom on this subject with a view to perhaps laying the groundwork for some agreement in the general assembly.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: There have been discussions with the authorities of the United Kingdom and there will continue to be further discussions, but the whole matter will probably be threshed out publicly in the discussion of the report of the international commission that has been set up.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: In view of the fact that certain South American countries such as Peru and Chile, I believe, have made unilateral declarations extending their territorial waters up to 200 miles, would the Prime Minister tell us whether or not, in view of the talks that have taken place, the government would consider suggesting that Canada's territorial waters extend beyond the 12-mile limit?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext:
No, I do not
think we would venture to claim that the territorial waters extended beyond the 12-mile limit. We would not think there would

be very much chance of having that recognized internationally, in spite of the declarations that have been made by some of the South American countries.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: May I ask the Prime Minister what the stand of the government is with regard to Hecate strait?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: I cannot make any formal statement. There are these several questions about which we do not think it would be advisable to take a stand publicly that would be apt to be controversial before there is this opportunity to have a general discussion of the report of this international commission of experts.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: I take it from what the Prime Minister has said that at this United Nations meeting the Canadian government is going to put forward the suggestion that foreign draggers stay outside of our 12-mile limit.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: There will be qualifications to that attitude because of the historic rights that have to be recognized with respect to the waters bordering our shores.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Does that mean that anybody now fishing within our 12-mile limit is going to be allowed to continue to do so?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: No, Mr. Chairman, it does not mean that and it does not mean the contrary. It does not make any assertion whatsoever in that regard. That matter will be considered when there has been a sufficient recognition of the 12-mile limit for territorial waters.

subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: Then could the Prime Minister just say simply what it does mean?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
subtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING REGISTRATION, CERTIFICATES, ETC.
speechtext: It means that the question is not yet one that is determined satisfactorily under international law.
